analyst_view.overall: Early view: Tottenham's three-game league winning run ended with a 1-0 defeat at Leeds, and Roberto De Zerbi is still without Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall and Mykhailo Mudryk; one report has Savinho due back for this game. Ipswich, 14th under Gary O'Neil, lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, two of them Tottenham's. I lean lower: Spurs failed to score at Leeds, several creative players are out with knee injuries and James Maddison's fitness has been a worry. Ipswich's last defeat was only a narrow 2-1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, seven of them for Spurs. That fits a De Zerbi side that keeps the ball against an Ipswich team likely to defend deep, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Spurs had Van de Ven, Porro and Tonali booked at Leeds, plus De Zerbi himself, so they are not shy of cards, but Ipswich picked up only two against Bournemouth. With no referee named, I stay with the numbers.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, 19 of them Tottenham's. De Zerbi's teams take a lot of the ball, which supports a high count, but the injuries to Simons and Odobert remove two attacking options. The two effects roughly cancel out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Spurs did not score at Leeds and their attack is thinner than usual, so more of their shots may come from distance or be blocked.
